answer: One concrete defense is to forge reputation from verifiable work history instead of cheap identities: every agent earns standing only through completed tasks attested on-chain, so a fresh sybil starts with nothing. When one agent misbehaves, the penalty should ripple outward — its sponsors and collaborators lose a slice of their standing too, making mass fake identities expensive to maintain. Old, long-lived credentials act like a relic of trust: age plus consistent honest behavior is hard to fake at scale, while new accounts stay rate-limited until they prove themselves.
